citation_reviews.supported_claim: Bamboo structures suppress suitable grain-boundary diffusion but require process/material conditions and may lose benefit to self-heating or interface diffusion.
citation_reviews.detail: Verified §4.2 and Fig.4.1. The notes correctly avoid claiming the aluminum result transfers directly to ordinary copper.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Via-above/below damage volumes and reservoir effects depend on geometry, material boundaries, current direction and mechanical confinement.
citation_reviews.detail: Checked §§4.4–4.5; source/sink reservoir effects may oppose, especially with reversing current and low-k surroundings. No published factor is turned into a universal rule.

corrections.after: For a point heater depositing power P at the flat surface of a homogeneous, isotropic, semi-infinite medium with constant conductivity k, assume the remaining surface is adiabatic and T approaches T<sub>∞</sub> far away. Hemispherical symmetry gives outward heat flux P/(2πr²). Fourier’s law then gives dT/dr = −P/(2πkr²), and integration from r to infinity yields ΔT(r) = T(r) − T<sub>∞</sub> = P/(2πkr). This is the handbook’s derivation under those boundary conditions; it is not asserted to be an equation printed in the supplied books. The 2π factor differs from the 4π factor for a point source in an unbounded full space. Philis uses this half-space approximation with a floor on r near the source.

theory_records.title: Area and distance contributions to MOS pair mismatch
theory_records.claim: For the characterized equal-device pair model, variance is approximated by A_P²/(WL)+S_P²D².
theory_records.locator: Analysis, Eq.(1), printed pp.327–328
theory_records.assumptions: Many small additive local events with correlation distance much smaller than device dimensions, plus a fitted long-range component; process/parameter-specific coefficients. A refers to the pair-difference statistic here. A single-device coefficient requires its own convention conversion.

theory_records.title: Edge variation prevents a universal area-only beta law
theory_records.claim: Current-factor variance contains width-edge, length-edge, mobility and oxide terms before an approximate A_beta²/(WL) reduction.
theory_records.locator: Matching of MOS transistors, Eq.(3), printed p.328
theory_records.assumptions: Area-dependent contribution only; same defined process parameters; authors say simplification becomes less valid as W and L decrease.

theory_records.title: Orientation evidence is process-specific
theory_records.claim: The studied 90-degree rotation affected current-factor mismatch and varied by wafer/batch; this experiment did not establish arbitrary transform equivalence.
theory_records.locator: Orientation discussion, Fig.3(d), printed pp.328–330
theory_records.assumptions: 2.5µm n-well CMOS experiment; no universal rotational/reflection/source-drain symmetry rule for another process.

theory_records.title: Use independent physical causes in mismatch models
theory_records.claim: Treating threshold and gain-factor mismatch as independent can double count an underlying oxide-thickness fluctuation; bias and geometry matter.
theory_records.locator: Section II, Table I and discussion surrounding Eqs.(4)–(6), printed p.451
theory_records.assumptions: Do not apply this critique as a prohibition on all calibrated local empirical fits; inspect whether the statistical basis and correlations are already handled.

theory_records.title: Propagate mismatch with covariance and circuit sensitivity
theory_records.claim: For a first-order expansion Δe≈JΔp, Var(e)≈J C Jᵀ; Drennan Eq.(8) is the independent-parameter special case.
theory_records.locator: Section II, Eqs.(7)–(11), printed p.452
theory_records.assumptions: Small perturbations around the specified bias/geometry, valid compact model, and covariance C for the same physical variables; nonlinear tails need additional treatment.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Cov(JΔp)=J Cov(Δp) Jᵀ. If C is diagonal, this reduces to Σ_i (∂e/∂p_i)² σ_i², matching Eq.(8).

theory_records.title: Fixed-current width can trade averaging against sensitivity
theory_records.claim: In a long-channel saturation, threshold-only toy model at fixed current, relative current variance from threshold mismatch is proportional to 1/L² and independent of W.
theory_records.locator: Eq.(9) and §III.A Geometry and Bias Interrelationship, printed pp.452,454
theory_records.assumptions: This is an illustrative derivation, not a modern compact-model law; ignore mobility/edge/series/short-channel contributions and use the stated area coefficient. Recheck headroom.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: σ²(ΔI/I)≈4A²/(WL Vov²), while Vov²=2IL/(μCox W); substitution gives 2A² μCox/(I L²). The source supports the more general observation that changing W changes both physical variation and sensitivity.

theory_records.title: Splitting preserves ideal total-area random mismatch
theory_records.claim: Four independent 20µm-wide units can reproduce the ideal mismatch of one 80µm-wide device at the same length; there is no free fixed-total-width averaging gain.
theory_records.locator: §III.C Multiple-Unit Devices, printed p.455
theory_records.assumptions: Width effects and altered electrical/parasitic context neglected; compare equal total width, not an array with one small unit. Circuit-role differences are separately shown in Table III.

theory_records.title: Substrate coupling is a complete contact-network problem
theory_records.claim: Injected substrate current paths depend on injector, receiver, other contacts, doping profile and backplate potential; taps/wells may inject return noise.
theory_records.locator: §1.1 and Chapter 2 §§2–3, printed pp.2,15–17
theory_records.assumptions: State injector mechanisms, reference connections and receiving impedance/body bias; a distance-only pair model omits third-contact loading.

theory_records.title: Electroquasistatic substrate equation and boundaries
theory_records.claim: Conductive and displacement currents obey ∇·(σ∇φ)+∂t[∇·(ε∇φ)]=0; the resistive limit and explicit contact/edge/interface boundaries determine the model.
theory_records.locator: Chapter 3 §2 Electromagnetic Formulation, Eqs.(3.1)–(3.3), printed pp.22–23
theory_records.assumptions: Electroquasistatic continuum regime. Resistive approximation requires ε/σ small relative to times of interest; contact equipotential and insulating/grounded boundaries must match the physical setup.

theory_records.title: Isolation includes loading and sign convention
theory_records.claim: The book defines contact isolation as V_receiver/V_injector; it depends on contact capacitance, backside impedance, frequency and receiver load, not only substrate resistance.
theory_records.locator: Chapter 8 §2 Characterizing Isolation and §4 Effects of Load Impedance, printed pp.101–102,111–112
theory_records.assumptions: Use a specified source/reference/loading convention. A negative-dB transfer and a positive attenuation magnitude have opposite reported signs.

theory_records.title: Separation can saturate in low-resistivity substrates
theory_records.claim: Finite backplate impedance can make isolation approximately independent of further contact separation in the book’s low-resistivity examples.
theory_records.locator: §8.2.1 Low-Resistivity Substrates, Figs.8.6–8.7; contrast §8.2.2, printed pp.102–107
theory_records.assumptions: Depends on epitaxial profile, area, frequency and backplate connection. Do not use its multiple-of-epitaxial-thickness example as a universal spacing rule.

theory_records.title: Guard-ring return and observation reference matter
theory_records.claim: A ring can worsen received noise through finite/noisy grounding; internal versus external signal reference and ring width/location change the result.
theory_records.locator: §8.6.1 Grounding Schemes and §8.6.2 Optimization of Guard Ring Widths, Figs.8.16–8.23, printed pp.116–124
theory_records.assumptions: The numerical studies use specific high-resistivity substrates and lumped package models. Compare actual reference voltage and include ring-return inductance and pickup.

theory_records.title: Buried shields have distinct mechanisms and limits
theory_records.claim: Conductive shields provide an alternate current return, dielectric isolation raises impedance, and buried opposite-type wells combine junction isolation with conductive shielding.
theory_records.locator: §8.9 Buried Substrate Shields, Figs.8.27–8.30, printed pp.128–133
theory_records.assumptions: The process must support the structure and bias. Conductive return impedance, finite shield resistivity, junction capacitance and frequency limit isolation.

theory_records.title: Differential substrate error is transfer imbalance
theory_records.claim: In a linear receiver difference, v_diff=(H1−H2)v_aggressor; equal common-mode transfer cancels only while the two complete paths and receiver responses match.
theory_records.locator: §8.3 Improving Isolation Using Differential Circuits, Figs.8.9–8.10, printed pp.107–111
theory_records.assumptions: Complex transfer functions with common reference. The source explicitly studies a 5% receiving-capacitor mismatch; phase, loading and circuit mismatch must remain included.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Subtract v1=H1 va and v2=H2 va. A 1% relative imbalance of a 0.01 transfer gives 10^-4 differential transfer only for the stated approximately equal-phase case.

theory_records.title: Local substrate-noise budgets need phase and sensitivity
theory_records.claim: Local noise generators permit performance-to-parasitic budget generation; the PLL example shows jitter depends on the phase of injection relative to transitions.
theory_records.locator: Chapter 5 §§1–3, Eqs.(5.1)–(5.5), §5.3 case study, printed pp.47–53,58
theory_records.assumptions: Local linearization or explicitly maximized sensitivity over a defined interval; source waveform/phase assumptions and circuit operating state must be retained. Shared budget allocation is not unique.

theory_records.title: Migration damage is flux divergence and coupled driving forces
theory_records.claim: Electrical, thermal and stress driving forces produce atomic flux; accumulation/depletion and coupled heating/stress determine vulnerable regions.
theory_records.locator: §2.2 and §2.5, especially Eqs.(2.15)–(2.18), printed pp.18,35–43
theory_records.assumptions: Material paths, interface boundary conditions, temperature and mechanical state matter; average current density alone is not a damage-location model.

theory_records.title: Black law describes a calibrated median
theory_records.claim: t50=C j^-n exp(Ea/kT) is a generalized empirical median-lifetime relation; a product reliability target also needs mission profile and failure statistics.
theory_records.assumptions: Same characterized process, geometry, mechanism, temperature/current range and failure criterion. Median is not low-failure-probability lifetime of every segment; do not extrapolate across mechanism changes.

theory_records.title: Current metrics are not interchangeable
theory_records.claim: RMS, effective/directional average and peak currents correspond to different mechanisms; all applicable dimensioning limits must be considered.
theory_records.locator: §2.4.3 and §3.3.1 Current Types, printed pp.29–32,70–71
theory_records.assumptions: RMS heating assumes resistance treated consistently; self-healing depends on characterized waveform/frequency/material behavior. Zero signed average does not imply zero damage.

theory_records.title: Topology and current-aware wire area
theory_records.claim: Signed terminal-current bounds/scenarios determine tree segment demand; current-driven planning can minimize required interconnect area rather than only length.
theory_records.assumptions: For transient cut sums include relevant interconnect shunt currents; retain mode/correlation assumptions. Meshes require a network current-sharing solution. The handbook’s exact waveform sum is a KCL expression, distinct from the book’s equivalent-current bounds.

theory_records.title: The metal path includes terminals and manufactured cross-section
theory_records.claim: Width must meet the largest applicable current/manufacturing requirement; pin landing regions and internal pin geometry need ampacity verification.
theory_records.assumptions: Application-robust per-layer rules, conducting thickness/width corrections and actual terminal current. mA/µm and A/cm² are distinct rule conventions. Via-temperature Eq.(3.25) requires the separate caveat in P22.

theory_records.title: Via capacity depends on current sharing
theory_records.claim: Via arrays at direction changes can overload inner cuts; equal cut count is not equal maximum-cut utilization.
theory_records.locator: §4.6 Multiple Vias, especially §4.6.4 and Figs.4.25–4.29, printed pp.122–128
theory_records.assumptions: Include both connected metal layers, contact resistances and reservoir/mechanical consequences. The source’s geometric equalization examples are conditional templates, not universal equal-sharing proofs.

theory_records.title: Correct fixed-lifetime temperature scaling
theory_records.claim: For unchanged Black parameters and target lifetime, j_allow(T)/j_allow(Tref)=exp[(Ea/(nk))(1/T−1/Tref)]. Required identical-via count grows as the inverse capacity factor.
theory_records.locator: Derived from Eq.(3.8); compare printed Eqs.(3.25)–(3.26), printed pp.81,89
theory_records.assumptions: Absolute Kelvin temperatures, positive Ea and n, unchanged geometry/failure mechanism. Printed via-count equations exhibit apparent inverse-factor inconsistency; no publisher erratum or foundry qualification was established.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Set C j_T^-n exp(Ea/kT)=C j_ref^-n exp(Ea/kTref), take logarithms, solve n ln(j_T/j_ref)=Ea/k(1/T−1/Tref). A smaller per-via allowable current requires more cuts, not fewer.

theory_records.title: Blech protection requires a physical stress/diffusion domain
theory_records.claim: The one-dimensional balance gives |jL|crit=ΩΔσ/(e|Z*|ρ), subject to confinement, boundary and failure assumptions; void-growth saturation is a distinct criterion.
theory_records.locator: §4.3, Eq.(4.1), discussion of Eq.(4.2); §4.5.1 neighboring segments, printed pp.105–108,111,115,118
theory_records.assumptions: Physical boundaries and material flow, not arbitrary route vertices. Simple isolated segment model; branched/reservoir structures and transients require additional analysis. A safe-looking steady state is not proof of a damage-free transition.

theory_records.title: Half-space thermal spreading is a derived ideal model
theory_records.claim: For a surface point heater in a homogeneous isotropic semi-infinite body with an otherwise adiabatic surface and fixed far-field temperature, ΔT=P/(2πkr).
theory_records.locator: Fourier-law basis: §8.2.7 Thermal Gradients, Eq.(8.22), printed p.385. The half-space result is derived in the handbook, not printed as this equation in the book.
theory_records.assumptions: Constant k, steady state, hemispherical spreading, ideal point source, no finite die/package/layer effects. Singular near-source field requires finite-source treatment or labeled regularization.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Conservation on a hemisphere gives heat flux P/(2πr²). Fourier law gives dT/dr=−P/(2πkr²); integrate from r to infinity where T=T∞. Full unbounded space instead has 4π. The transient PDE adds local energy storage to the same flux balance.

theory_records.title: Centroid temperature needs four assumptions
theory_records.claim: A device’s average temperature equals its active-area centroid temperature only under the stated active-area, equal-contribution, linear electrical-temperature and linear spatial-temperature assumptions.
theory_records.locator: §8.2.7 Centroids, followed by Eq.(8.23), printed pp.386–387
theory_records.assumptions: Package and power conditions determine the field. Unequal electrical weighting, finite nonlinear fields or nonlinear device temperature dependence require more detailed evaluation. The handbook’s general Σs_i ΔT_i is a first-order sensitivity extension.

unresolved.detail: The internal monotonicity inconsistency was independently confirmed from the supplied printed equations and Black-law algebra. No external publisher erratum was checked. Keep the wording apparent inconsistency.

The sources do not supply an actual target-PDK mismatch covariance, EM deck, thermal/package network, substrate profile or activity model. Notes correctly identify these as required inputs; their numerical examples are illustrative.

This is a claim-level audit of the teaching content and citations. It is not independent reproduction of every cited experiment, every book numerical solver, or the substrate appendix’s asymptotic convergence proofs. Coverage links are navigation, not certified theory.

material_omissions_addressed: Dynamic tree current cut sums need shunt/displacement loads.
Instantaneous terminal electrical power includes stored energy and is not automatically heat.
Half-space thermal spreading needs adiabatic surface, far-field, homogeneity and point-source conditions.
Input-referral with gm needs absolute rather than normalized current mismatch.
remaining_coverage_boundary: Detailed latchup/protection physics is cross-referenced to the separate protection chapter. No additional unsupported process-specific constants were introduced.
